title: Trump's 'Chinese Virus' narrative
short_description: The Trump Administration systematically used the terms 'Chinese virus' or 'Wuhan virus', deflecting responsibility for the pandemic onto China and fuelling anti-Asian sentiment globally.
page_content: Trump Administration used the terms 'Chinese virus' or 'Wuhan virus', creating a blurred line about the origin of COVID-19 and accusing China of being responsible. It refers to the idea of a virus created by humans, specifically the narrative of COVID being born inside a laboratory complex in Wuhan.

title: China's claim that the U.S. Army brought COVID-19 to Wuhan
short_description: A Chinese disinformation narrative alleging that U.S. military personnel introduced the coronavirus to China, used to deflect blame for the outbreak.
emitter_actor: Chinese state media and foreign ministry spokesperson
page_content: Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Zhao Lijian claimed in March 2020 that the US military might have brought COVID-19 to Wuhan. The claim circulated during the early pandemic and later reappeared in amplified form around the Fort Detrick narrative.

title: US Pentagon secret anti-vax campaign in Philippines
short_description: During the COVID pandemic, the US Defense Department launched a covert campaign using fake social media accounts to undermine trust in China's Sinovac vaccine among Filipino audiences.
page_content: Given China's influence over the Philippines, the US launched a campaign through fake social media accounts to spread fear of China's vaccines. Using hashtags such as #ChinaAngVirus, the campaign aimed to amplify contention surrounding COVID-19 vaccines and undermine Sinovac.

title: Brazilian election disinformation campaign (2022)
short_description: Bolsonaro-aligned networks spread election integrity disinformation across Brazil and Latin America ahead of the October 2022 presidential election.
page_content: Bolsonaro-aligned networks targeted Brazilian voters with election integrity disinformation, framing Lula as a communist threat and casting doubt on Brazil's electronic voting system.

title: Russian interference in the 2016 US election
short_description: A coordinated influence operation by the Internet Research Agency targeting US voters through fake accounts, divisive content and political messaging across multiple platforms.
page_content: The Internet Research Agency, a Russian 'troll factory', ran a sustained influence operation targeting American voters. The campaign exploited divisive social issues, created fake grassroots movements, and specifically targeted African-American communities, progressive voters, and conservative bases to deepen political polarisation.
